summary: The article accurately describes the new SEBI nomination rules for Demat accounts and mutual funds, effective September 1, 2026, and highlights key changes and benefits for investors.

claims.claim: SEBI issued a circular on May 29, 2026, outlining these revised nomination rules.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the SEBI circular date as May 29, 2026.

claims.claim: The most crucial part is that these new rules will come into effect from September 1, 2026.
claims.note: The effective date of the new rules is consistently stated as September 1, 2026, across various sources.

claims.claim: If you open a new Demat account or mutual fund folio... as a single holder on or after September 1, 2026, you must either provide nomination details or formally declare that you choose *not* to nominate anyone.
claims.note: This is a core aspect of the new rules, confirmed by multiple sources.

claims.claim: If you submit a physical nomination form with your regular signature, you no longer need a witness signature. A witness is only required if you use a thumb impression instead of a signature.
claims.note: This simplification of the physical nomination process is widely reported.

claims.claim: You can nominate up to three individuals for your Demat account or mutual fund folio. If you name multiple nominees but don't specify their share, the investments will be divided equally among them by default.
claims.note: The allowance of up to three nominees and the default equal distribution are confirmed.

claims.claim: Depository participants and mutual fund registrars will send you bi-annual reminders (twice a year) via email and SMS if you haven't nominated anyone or formally opted out. They will also show pop-up messages on their apps or websites.
claims.note: The provision for bi-annual reminders and pop-up messages is mentioned in several sources.

claims.claim: This new circular replaces all previous SEBI circulars related to nominations in Demat accounts and mutual fund folios, creating a single, clearer framework.
claims.note: The circular supersedes previous SEBI circulars on nomination.

claims.claim: The official SEBI circular (SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-3/P/CIR/2026/12676) dated May 29, 2026, is usually available on the SEBI website under the "Circulars" section.
claims.note: The circular number and date are correct and it is available on the SEBI website.

article_title: Your Investments Just Got Simpler: New Nomination Rules for Demat Accounts & Mutual Funds
